title: Weakly associated primes after flat finitely presented algebra base change
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] which is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and let $M$ be any $R$-module. For a commutative ring $T$ and $T$-module $P$, write $\operatorname{WeakAss}_T(P)$ for the primes minimal among the prime ideals containing $\operatorname{Ann}_T(x)=\{a\in T:ax=0\}$ for some $x\in P$; and let $\operatorname{Ass}_T(P)$ mean the exact-annihilator associated primes [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime, $\mathfrak p$ its inverse image in $R$, $C=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and $\overline{\mathfrak q}\subset C$ the corresponding fibre prime (the prime whose inverse image in $S$ is $\mathfrak q$) [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection]. Here $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and $M\otimes_RS$ is an $S$-module through its second factor. Then
$$\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_S(M\otimes_RS)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\bigl(\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_R(M)\ \text{and}\ \overline{\mathfrak q}\in\operatorname{Ass}_C(C)\bigr).$$
There is no Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ or finite generation hypothesis on $M$.

source.place: Tag 05IG, lemma-weak-bourbaki-pre, statement at lines 3751-3774, specialized to N=S (a free S-module of rank one); tag checked in tags/tags. https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05IG

proof.text: We first record the localization bookkeeping used below. If $U$ is a multiplicative set in a ring $T$ and $\mathfrak t\cap U=\varnothing$, then $(U^{-1}T)_{U^{-1}\mathfrak t}=T_{\mathfrak t}$ and $(U^{-1}P)_{U^{-1}\mathfrak t}=P_{\mathfrak t}$: the inverse maps on fractions send $(a/u)/(b/v)$ to $av/(ub)$ and conversely. Thus the local radical-annihilator criterion [lem-sc-weakass-localization] gives $\mathfrak t\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_T(P)$ iff $U^{-1}\mathfrak t\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_{U^{-1}T}(U^{-1}P)$. We use this both for principal localization in $S$ and for localizing the base at $\mathfrak p$. The fibre $C$ is a finite-type algebra over the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$: substitute the images of coefficients in a finite presentation of $S$. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian. Every prime of $C$ is therefore finitely generated, and [lem-sc-ass-weakass-fg-prime] identifies its weakly associated primes with its exact-annihilator associated primes. The same observations apply to every fibre ring below.

source.place: Tag 05IG, localization criterion and the Noetherian fibre rings used throughout

proof.text: Write $Q=\overline{\mathfrak q}$. The set $E=\operatorname{Ass}_C(C)$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-primes-finite]. For each $\mathfrak r\in E$ not contained in $Q$ choose $a_{\mathfrak r}\in\mathfrak r\setminus Q$ and multiply these elements. The product $a$ lies in every such $\mathfrak r$ and is outside $Q$; an empty product is $1$. Write $a=b/s$ in $C=S_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak p}$ with $b\in S$, $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$, and put $g=b$. Multiplication by the unit $s$ preserves membership in each prime, so $g\notin\mathfrak q$ and its image belongs to all the unwanted primes. Replace $S$ by $S_g$ and $\mathfrak q$ by $\mathfrak qS_g$. Step 1 preserves both the assertion about $\mathfrak q$ and the fibre-associated assertion. In this new fibre every associated prime contracts to an associated prime of the old fibre contained in $Q$. The new algebra is still finitely presented (adjoin $t$ with $gt=1$) and flat: localize the injection obtained by tensoring with the original flat $S$, using [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. We retain $R,S,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q,C,Q$ for these localized data.

source.place: Tag 05IG, choice of g via lemma-weak-bourbaki-pre-pre (Tag 05IF); the product and denominator argument are written out

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-algebra-etale-projective-neighborhood] to obtain the pointed etale square $R\to R^{\prime}$, $S\to S^{\prime}$ with primes $\mathfrak p^{\prime},\mathfrak q^{\prime}$ and projective $R^{\prime}$-module $S^{\prime}$. Put $M^{\prime}=M\otimes_R R^{\prime}$, $W=M\otimes_R S$, $W^{\prime}=M^{\prime}\otimes_{R^{\prime}}S^{\prime}=W\otimes_S S^{\prime}$, $C^{\prime}=S^{\prime}\otimes_{R^{\prime}}\kappa(\mathfrak p^{\prime})$, and $Q^{\prime}=\overline{\mathfrak q^{\prime}}$. The displayed identification sends $(m\otimes r^{\prime})\otimes s^{\prime}$ to $m\otimes r^{\prime}s^{\prime}$, with inverse $m\otimes s^{\prime}\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes s^{\prime}$. By [lem-trf-etale-weakass-invariance], weak association of $\mathfrak q$ to $W$ is equivalent to that of $\mathfrak q^{\prime}$ to $W^{\prime}$, and weak association of $\mathfrak p$ to $M$ is equivalent to that of $\mathfrak p^{\prime}$ to $M^{\prime}$. Apply the same theorem to the etale map $C\to C^{\prime}$ and then the Noetherian conversion of Step 1: $Q\in\operatorname{Ass}_C(C)$ iff $Q^{\prime}\in\operatorname{Ass}_{C^{\prime}}(C^{\prime})$.

source.place: Tag 05IG, first two proof paragraphs, etale diagram and three equivalences

proof.text: Every $\mathfrak r^{\prime}\in\operatorname{Ass}_{C^{\prime}}(C^{\prime})$ contracts, by the etale weak-assassin theorem and Step 1, to an associated prime $\mathfrak r$ of $C$. The choice of $g$ ensures $\mathfrak r\subseteq Q$. Also there are no strict inclusions between primes of $C^{\prime}$ with the same contraction to $C$: if $\mathfrak a^{\prime}\subseteq\mathfrak b^{\prime}$ both contract to $\mathfrak a$, then [lem-weil-pbc-etale-prime-generates-maximal] says $\mathfrak a C^{\prime}_{\mathfrak b^{\prime}}=\mathfrak b^{\prime}C^{\prime}_{\mathfrak b^{\prime}}$, and the intermediate prime $\mathfrak a^{\prime}C^{\prime}_{\mathfrak b^{\prime}}$ must equal it; contraction back gives equality. Consequently, whenever $Q^{\prime}$ is associated, it is maximal among the associated primes of $C^{\prime}$: any associated prime containing it contracts to a prime both containing and contained in $Q$, and hence equals it.

source.place: Tag 05IG, key observation and maximality of the selected fibre-associated prime

proof.text: For the first implication suppose initially that $Q$ is not associated. Then $Q^{\prime}$ is not associated by Step 3. No associated prime $\mathfrak r^{\prime}$ of $C^{\prime}$ can contain $Q^{\prime}$: contraction and Step 4 would force equality. Apply finite prime avoidance [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] to $Q^{\prime}$ and the finite set of associated primes [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-primes-finite]. We obtain $a\in Q^{\prime}$ outside their union, hence multiplication by $a$ on $C^{\prime}$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-module-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes]. If that finite set is empty, take $a=0$ and use the same zero-divisor statement. Since $C^{\prime}=S^{\prime}_{\mathfrak p^{\prime}}/\mathfrak p^{\prime}S^{\prime}_{\mathfrak p^{\prime}}$, multiply $a$ by a nonzero residue-field scalar to obtain the image of an $a^{\prime}\in\mathfrak q^{\prime}$; this does not change injectivity. The lift lies in $\mathfrak q^{\prime}$ because $Q^{\prime}$ contracts to it.

source.place: Tag 05IG, paragraph beginning Suppose that the fibre prime is not associated

proof.text: Put $A=R^{\prime}_{\mathfrak p^{\prime}}$ and $B=S^{\prime}_{\mathfrak p^{\prime}}$. The module $B$ is projective over $A$: localize the splitting of $S^{\prime}$ as a summand of a free $R^{\prime}$-module, obtaining a splitting into a free $A$-module. A free module is flat because tensoring with it is a direct sum of copies of the input map; its direct summands are flat by restricting that injection to the summand. Apply [lem-trf-local-universal-injective-residue] to multiplication by $a^{\prime}$ on $B$; its residue-field map is multiplication by $a$ on $C^{\prime}$. It is universally injective over $A$, hence injective on $M^{\prime}_{\mathfrak p^{\prime}}\otimes_A B$ and, after exact localization, on $W^{\prime}_{\mathfrak q^{\prime}}$. This prevents weak association at $\mathfrak q^{\prime}$: an element with annihilator radical the maximal ideal would be killed by a power of $a^{\prime}$, and injectivity would force it to be zero. The local criterion and Step 3 give $\mathfrak q\notin\operatorname{WeakAss}_S(W)$. Thus for every $M$, weak association at $\mathfrak q$ implies fibre association at $Q$.

source.place: Tag 05IG, universal injectivity argument proving the fibre condition

source.place: Tag 05IG, base weak-association argument, choice of z and its nonzero image

proof.text: The image of $g_f$ in $C^{\prime}$ avoids every associated prime: its contraction in $C$ is contained in $Q$ by Step 4, whereas $g_f\notin\mathfrak q$. The zero-divisor theorem makes multiplication by this image injective on $C^{\prime}$. As in Step 6, [lem-trf-local-universal-injective-residue] makes multiplication by $g_f$ universally injective on $S^{\prime}_{\mathfrak p^{\prime}}$ over $R^{\prime}_{\mathfrak p^{\prime}}$. Cancelling it in $g_f f^{n_f}z^{\prime}=0$ gives $f^{n_f}z^{\prime}=0$ for every $f\in\mathfrak p$. Since $\mathfrak p^{\prime}R^{\prime}_{\mathfrak p^{\prime}}=\mathfrak pR^{\prime}_{\mathfrak p^{\prime}}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-prime-generates-maximal], the radical of the $R^{\prime}_{\mathfrak p^{\prime}}$-annihilator of $z^{\prime}$ is its maximal ideal: it contains the generators from $\mathfrak p$, and is proper because $z^{\prime}\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 05IG, cancellation of g_i and radical of the base annihilator

proof.text: The projective module $S^{\prime}_{\mathfrak p^{\prime}}$ is free over the local ring $R^{\prime}_{\mathfrak p^{\prime}}$ by [lem-trf-projective-over-local-free]. Expanding $z^{\prime}$ in this basis expresses it as a finite tuple of elements of $M^{\prime}_{\mathfrak p^{\prime}}$, at least one coordinate $v$ nonzero. Every base element whose power annihilates $z^{\prime}$ has that same power annihilating $v$; Step 8 therefore makes the radical of $\operatorname{Ann}(v)$ the maximal ideal. By [lem-sc-weakass-localization] this gives $\mathfrak p^{\prime}\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_{R^{\prime}}(M^{\prime})$, and by [lem-trf-etale-weakass-invariance] it gives $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_R(M)$. Steps 1--9 have now proved the entire forward implication for every flat finitely presented algebra and every module, without using the reverse implication.

source.place: Tag 05IG, free-module coordinate argument finishing the forward implication

proof.text: For the reverse implication assume $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_R(M)$ and $Q\in\operatorname{Ass}_C(C)$. Perform Steps 2--4. They preserve these assumptions, make $S^{\prime}$ projective over $R^{\prime}$, and make $Q^{\prime}$ maximal among the associated primes of $C^{\prime}$. Localize the base at $\mathfrak p^{\prime}$ and rename the data $(A,\mathfrak m)$, $B$, $L$, $\mathfrak b$, $D=B/\mathfrak mB$, and $\overline{\mathfrak b}$. Thus $A$ is local, $B$ is a projective $A$-module and a finitely presented $A$-algebra, $\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_A(L)$, and $\overline{\mathfrak b}$ is maximal in $\operatorname{Ass}_D(D)$. These are the same fibres because tensoring a localized presentation with the residue field does not change it; projectivity follows by localizing its splitting. Step 1 preserves the relevant weak association. It suffices to prove $\mathfrak b\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_B(L\otimes_A B)$, since Step 1 and the etale equivalence of Step 3 then return to the original rings.

source.place: Tag 05IG, reductions (1)--(5) in the reverse implication

proof.text: The local criterion [lem-sc-weakass-localization] gives $y\in L$ such that $I=\operatorname{Ann}_A(y)$ has radical $\mathfrak m$. The map $A/I\to L$, $\bar a\mapsto ay$, is injective. Tensoring it with $B$ embeds $B/IB$ into $L\otimes_A B$, since a projective module is a summand of a free module and tensoring such a summand preserves injections, as explained in Step 6. The same splitting, tensored with $A/I$, shows $B/IB$ is projective over $A/I$. The fibre $D$ is Noetherian by Step 1, so write $\overline{\mathfrak b}=(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_n)$ and lift the generators to $h_i\in B$; then $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak mB+(h_1,\ldots,h_n)$. These are quotient lifts along the surjection $B\to D$, with no claim that $\mathfrak b$ itself is finitely generated.

source.place: Tag 05IG, choice of y, its annihilator I and generators of the fibre prime

proof.text: Consider the $A/I$-linear map $\Psi:B/IB\to(B/IB)^{\oplus n}$, $z\mapsto(h_1z,\ldots,h_nz)$. Both modules are projective over $A/I$ by the splitting in Step 11. Tensoring with $A/\mathfrak m$ gives the same multiplication-vector map on $D$. It has a nonzero kernel element: an exact-annihilator witness for $\overline{\mathfrak b}\in\operatorname{Ass}_D(D)$ is killed by every $\bar h_i$. Every element of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/I$ of $A/I$ is nilpotent since $\sqrt I=\mathfrak m$. If $\Psi$ were injective, [lem-trf-nil-local-projective-injection-pure] would make its residue-field tensor injective, a contradiction. Choose $0\ne z\in\ker\Psi$ and let $J=\operatorname{Ann}_B(z)$. We have $IB\subseteq J$ and $h_i\in J$. For every $a\in\mathfrak m$ some power belongs to $I$, so $\mathfrak mB\subseteq\sqrt J$. Therefore $\mathfrak b\subseteq\sqrt J$. This argument includes $n=0$, when $\Psi$ has zero target.

source.place: Tag 05IG, the map Psi and application of More on Algebra Tag 05GQ

proof.text: Since $z\ne0$, $J$ is proper. Choose a prime $\mathfrak s$ minimal over $J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal]. Then $\mathfrak s$ is weakly associated to $B/IB$ by its defining witness $z$, contains $\mathfrak b$, and contracts to $\mathfrak m$ because $\mathfrak m$ is maximal. Apply only the forward implication already proved in Steps 1--9 to the flat finitely presented algebra $A\to B$ and the module $A/I$; its tensor with $B$ is $B/IB$. This yields $\overline{\mathfrak s}\in\operatorname{Ass}_D(D)$. It contains $\overline{\mathfrak b}$, so maximality from Step 10 gives equality. The fibre-prime bijection [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] gives $\mathfrak s=\mathfrak b$. Thus $\mathfrak b$ is minimal over $\operatorname{Ann}_B(z)$. Under the injection $B/IB\to L\otimes_A B$ of Step 11 its annihilator stays exactly $J$ (an element kills its image if and only if it kills $z$), proving weak association to $L\otimes_A B$. The equivalences of Step 10 prove the required reverse implication in the original rings.

source.place: Tag 05IG, final paragraph; apply the previously proved forward direction, not the equivalence

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q63-5a5878ef1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole split. It is Stacks 05IG (flat.tex 3750-3980) with N=S, built on 05IF, 05FP, 05ID and More on Algebra 05GM/05GN/05GP/05GQ, all checked at their labels in tags/tags. The item statement, stmt_deps and blueprint field match the base exactly. The worker's source-error note is correct: 05IG writes S'⊗κ(q') where it needs κ(p'), and WeakAss_S(M) where it needs WeakAss_R(M). Steps 1-13 hold. Step 2 (separating element g), step 4 (key observation; no inclusions among étale-fibre primes, via etale-prime-generates-maximal), steps 5-6 (regular element and universal injectivity), steps 8-9 (cancelling g_f, coordinate argument) and steps 10-13 (cyclic A/I reduction, Psi, minimal prime, forward direction reused without circularity) were each checked against the statements they cite. All three new nodes are true, smaller than the item, not duplicates and statement-only. lem-trf-etale-weakass-invariance (05FP, affine form) was tested on k->k x k and L=0. lem-trf-flat-algebra-etale-projective-neighborhood (05ID with F=O): I checked the fp permanence and that the fibre map C->C' is étale; on k->k[t] the projective module has infinite rank. lem-trf-nil-local-projective-injection-pure: a nil-maximal local ring is auto-associated, so 05GQ (1)=>(2) applies; tested on a field, k[eps], and the infinite-rank example after 05GQ is consistent. The off-unit tool_uses are generic algebra tools; I accept them. One C3 fault, repaired in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula/lem-trf-flat-tensor-weakass-fibre.json: step 7 used lem-sc-weakass-localization (which only gives some element) to get g_f f^n z=0 for the chosen z. The repaired step argues explicitly: Ann_{S_q}(z/1)=Ann_S(z)S_q, minimality makes qS_q the only prime containing it, its radical is qS_q by lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq (a Mathlib leaf), and clearing denominators gives g_f. I updated the uses, proof_deps and tool_uses to match. No statement changed and no node dropped.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
